runtime.execution: Delimited-continuation fibers over configurable OS-thread schedulers; IO polling, timers and optional preemption.
runtime.service_boundary: Runs inside a Guile application; does not own shared kernels, providers or an agent fabric.

summary: Composable choice/wrap operations and synchronous channels offer expressive concurrency; cancellation in this snapshot has a source-level coverage concern.

inspection.scope: Read run/spawn/cleanup, operation choice/suspension/cancellation, timers, concurrency design and channel/preemption/cancel-timer tests.
inspection.limits: No execution or full Guile/foreign-IO audit; distributed participants, persistent checkpoint and harness refit are outside role.

actions.name: run-fibers / spawn-fiber
actions.input: Initial thunk, parallelism, preemption hz, drain flag; child closure
actions.lifecycle: Default completion ends scheduler; drain waits for pending work.

actions.name: choice-operation / wrap-operation / perform-operation
actions.output: One selected result or suspension until ready
actions.lifecycle: Suspended fiber or blocking foreign thread; losing cancellation has noted defect.

actions.name: timer-operation / sleep-operation
actions.lifecycle: Cancelable wheel entry when callback reached.

evidence.claim: Schedulers support configurable parallelism/preemption; default returns when initial thunk finishes, while drain waits for pending work; auxiliary threads stop during unwind.
Fibers start next scheduler turn, capture dynamic state and may select parallel scheduler.
Choice flattens alternatives; wrap transforms results; suspend resumes captured continuation.
Named loop visits index zero without recursive advance; later losing alternatives are not traversed in this pinned source.
Timer uses internal elapsed time and cancellation removes wheel entry when its callback is invoked.
Blocking IO suspends fibers; foreign threads may block; fibers are in-process delimited continuations.

tests.oracle: Explicit equal-value assertions including rpc-fib 24 = 75025; termination-only pingpong is weaker.

tests.focus: Busy fibers progressing without cooperative IO yields.
tests.oracle: Two fibers alternate atomic counter parity; expected result 100. Test success is not bounded production cancellation.
After 200000 choices with timer first, heap must grow no more than 2x; placement does not cover later losing alternatives, allocator behavior affects oracle.

strengths: First-class operations compose communication, continuations and deadlines.
Explicit initial-thunk versus drain lifecycle informs honest ongoing-work boundaries.
limits: No durable restart/continuation transfer or agent policy provided.
Source concern: cancellation loop only checks index zero; position-specific test can miss later alternatives.
arconaut_questions: Can ordinary programs combine cancellation, IO and result routing without callback boilerplate?
A three-way choice test must assert every losing cancellation callback fires exactly once for each winner position.
